bundlingNotes: Rate Manual General Rules state: 'The rates shown are the all-inclusive title insurance fees and charges and includes both the risk portion and the service or work portion, but does not include charges for title search, surveys, escrow, closing services, settlement services, recording fees, other charges, or other monies advanced on behalf of an applicant.' This is a distinctive middle-ground structure -- unlike most states' pure risk-only premium, WFG's Rhode Island rate explicitly bundles some 'service or work portion' into the premium (similar in spirit to Tennessee's All-Inclusive Rate rule), while still excluding title search, escrow, and closing/settlement services as separate unregulated charges.

methodology: Driven via plain HTTP POST (Python requests.Session(), not WebFetch -- WebFetch's HTML-to-markdown conversion strips the raw hidden ASP.NET fields needed to replay the postback), following this project's existing FNF recipe documented in CALCULATORS.md: GET the county-selection page, POST the county (own __EVENTTARGET), POST btnGeneralNext=Next, POST TranType$ddl=PropertyPurchase, POST AmountPurchase$txt=500000 then AmountLoan1$txt=400000 (each with its own __EVENTTARGET), auto-answer the revealed Concurrent-rate-eligibility question Yes, then POST btnFinish=Finish for the final Rate Summary. One correction to the prior recipe write-up worth flagging: the page also renders a hidden 'ctl00$btnDummy' submit button used only for Enter-key submission -- a naive first-submit-button-found selector picks this dummy button instead of the real 'Next'/'Finish' button and silently fails to advance the flow; always filter submit-button candidates for the actual button's own name substring ('Next'/'Finish') rather than taking the first match. No personal-data fields exist anywhere in this flow.
